subject: RM_Skerrel

clauses_applied: A (n/a: invented RM_ creature, no canon entry)
B3 (no sibling keeps; lifestages share one texture)

measurements: all three 256x256 RGBA; alpha bbox south (17,17,239,238), east (8,50,248,206), north (10,12,245,243); zero alpha on every border pixel; ~1.4-1.7k semi-transparent edge pixels each (antialias, no visible halo in composite). Canvas 256 px vs drawSize 0.6 x 128 = 77 px: generous (D2).

verdicts.notes: C1: faces the viewer - head at the bottom with two orange compound eyes and mandibles toward camera, thorax then striped abdomen receding upward; a separate drawing, not the north rotated. Perspective is steep (abdomen shown near full length), acceptable for a 0.4-0.6 cell flyer. C2: same palette (leaf-green thorax, yellow/dark-green bands, glassy veined wings, dark brown legs) and span as north. D4: clean alpha, no backdrop/shadow/fragments. B2: at 32 px reads as a small yellow-striped wasp, clearly apart from ground. B1a: thin dark edge shading on legs only, no heavy keyline.

C1/C2: clean right-facing profile - head, eye and antennae at right, stinger at left; proportions and palette match south/north. Mirrored west (composite) reads correctly as left-facing, no asymmetric detail that breaks on mirror. D3/D4: widest facing but inside canvas, zero border alpha, no halo. E1/E2 + goal: plainly distinct from the Fire Wasp (that is a brown armour-scaled, amber-winged bulky insect; this is a slim green/yellow-banded wasp) - bespoke, not donor or script-drawn. Reads at 77 px and 32 px.

C1: rear view - head at top seen from behind with antennae, no eyes or mandibles visible; abdomen and stinger toward the viewer. C2: size, wing span and palette agree with south. D4: clean alpha. Reads at 32 px.

proposals: C1 could say what a small flyer's south/north perspective should be: both facings here are near-dorsal (abdomen shown near full length) and differ only by head end; I kept them because C1 only bans a rotated top-down view and these are separate drawings, but the brief does not decide how steep is too steep for flyers.
